meta.tagline: White villages on a volcano's rim, wine below, the sunset across

pills: Assyrtiko is one of the world's great whites

overview.title: Welcome to Santorini
overview.intro: As the ferry enters the caldera, the view catches you unprepared: white villages scattered like snow on the rim of three-hundred-metre lava walls. Santorini lives on the edge of an exploded volcano — its soil black, its wine sharp, its sunset world-famous. Yes, it's crowded; yes, it's expensive. But the moment you first sit on the caldera's edge, every objection falls silent. The art is finding the village square as well as the postcard.

local_word.definition: Doing a thing with your soul in it: Greek's untranslatable word. From the craftsman whitewashing the caldera houses by hand to the aunt simmering fava for hours — meraki is Santorini's secret of survival.

rules.title: Don't imprison the sunset in Oia
rules.description: Oia's castle is shoulder-to-shoulder at dusk. The same sun sets from Imerovigli, from Pyrgos, from the Akrotiri lighthouse — and there you'll find air to breathe and a stone to sit on.

rules.title: Don't ride the donkeys down the caldera
rules.description: The donkey rides on the old-port steps are misery for the animals; the ethics debate is settled. There is a cable car, and walking is free — photograph the donkeys, don't burden them.

rules.title: Verify the words 'caldera view' before booking
rules.description: The view that doubles the price is sometimes barely glimpsed past a neighbour's roof. Ask for real photos and the room's orientation before reserving; the viewless side is half the price and surprisingly lovely.

tip.label: The Santorini philosophy
tip.text: The most expensive thing on this island is a table with a view; the most precious is a stone wall with one. The second is free — with a supermarket Assyrtiko and some cheese you build the world's best restaurant yourself.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The island is small but its roads are narrow and its July is crowded; the transport plan decides the day's pleasure.

items.title: Arrival — port and airport
items.description: Ferries dock at Athinios; the climb out is a serpentine road needing bus or transfer. The airport is 15 minutes from Fira. For both, arrange summer transfers ahead — taxis are few.

items.title: KTEL buses — hub at Fira
items.description: All lines radiate from the Fira terminal: Oia, Perissa, Akrotiri, the port. Cheap and frequent but packed in summer; avoid rush hours with big luggage.

items.title: Renting a small car
items.description: The way to roam freely; but the roads are narrow and parking in Oia and Fira is a struggle. Choose a small car and respect the headlit bends at night.

items.title: Cable car and the caldera steps
items.description: The cable car links the old port and Fira in minutes; the 587-step stairway is a scenic workout. Give the donkey rides no custom.

items.title: The Fira–Oia caldera walk
items.description: The island's best 'transport': 10 km along the caldera's rim, 3–4 hours. It passes Imerovigli and Skaros; timed to reach Oia at sunset, it becomes legend.

callout.label: ATV warning
callout.text: Quad bikes are an island classic with a fat accident statistic on narrow roads; if you rent one, the helmet is non-negotiable and night riding is your no-go zone.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: On Santorini the address boils down to two words: caldera, or not? Both can be the right answer.

local_word.definition: A cave house carved into the volcanic rock: the essence of Santorini architecture. Cool, silent and vaulted — sleeping in a yposkafo is living the island from the inside.

items.name: Oia
items.description: The village of blue domes, windmills and that famous sunset: the honeymoon classic. Prices at their peak, lanes full by day; but owning Oia at 7 am is beyond price.

items.name: Imerovigli
items.description: The caldera's highest village: Oia's view, Fira's proximity, the night's silence. Skaros Rock at your doorstep; the caldera budget is often spent most wisely here.

items.name: Fira
items.description: The island's capital: bus terminal, restaurants, nightlife and the cable car. Easy reach everywhere at the price of crowds and noise; a sensible base for short stays.

items.name: Pyrgos
items.description: A hilltop kastelli village inland: narrow lanes, blue doors, real life far from caldera tourism. Next door to the wine country; fair prices, starry evenings.

items.name: Perissa / Perivolos
items.description: The long shore of black sand: beach bars, dive schools and half the caldera's prices. Cut out for the beach holiday + caldera day-trip formula.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Santorini's question is not the sun but the people per square metre.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Calm Caldera
items.subtitle: Spring · Walking weather, opening season
items.description: Ideal temperature for the Fira–Oia path, hotels open, crowds still manageable. The sea warms in June; the photographer's light is clean.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May do the caldera walk in the afternoon and enter Oia with the sunset: the season's finest finale.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Peak Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Full lanes, full glasses
items.description: The island at capacity: sunset sittings like ticketed shows, restaurants by reservation. Lovers of warm seas and nightlife come now — with patience and a budget.

callout.label: July–August warning
callout.text: Walking Oia's main lane at sunset hour is a 20-minute undertaking; either settle in two hours early or watch from another point.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Harvest Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, softening crowds
items.description: September is the island's secret peak: warm sea, golden light, harvest in the wineries. Toward late October the island takes a deep breath.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: In September winery tastings open up; land in harvest time and you'll taste among the grape baskets.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Island Itself
items.subtitle: Winter · Empty caldera, dramatic skies
items.description: Some hotels close and the island returns to its people: a stormy caldera, empty paths, tavernas by the fire. Not for comfort-seekers — for those who want the island naked.

callout.label: Winter tip
callout.text: Winter clouds don't ruin the sunset, they dramatise it; storm-watching from Imerovigli is the island's least-known luxury.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Volcanic soil gives little water and much character: Santorini's tomato is small, its wine sharp, its fava like silk.

local_word.definition: The white grape of the volcanic soil: mineral, acidic, a worldwide cult. The vines are pruned into basket shapes (kouloura) against the wind — see the vineyard before the glass.

items.name: Tomatokeftedes — tomato fritters
items.description: The tiny, intense tomatoes of the dry land become fritters with mint and onion: crisp outside, sunshine within. The island's signature meze.

items.name: Fava — Santorini style
items.description: The island's yellow split peas (PDO protected) become a silken purée, topped with capers, onion and lemon. It looks simple and stays unforgettable.

items.name: The white aubergine
items.description: Sweet, seedless and grown only here: grilled or in salad, the star of the summer menus.

items.name: Grilled fish at Ammoudi
items.description: In the tiny port below Oia the tavernas sit at the water's edge: the day's fish, white tablecloths, red cliffs. Book before sunset hour.

items.name: A winery tasting
items.description: Santo, Venetsanos, Sigalas: the caldera-view tasting terraces are the island's best 'museums'. Start with Assyrtiko, close with sweet Vinsanto.

items.name: Melitinia with Vinsanto
items.description: The little Easter-born cheese sweets and the wine of sun-dried grapes: the island's sweet farewell.

callout.label: The view-tax rule
callout.text: A caldera-view table adds a fifty percent 'view tax' to dinner. The formula: eat lunch on a village square, buy the view with a glass at dusk — order the sunset, not the dinner.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Behind the postcard there is another island: quiet, volcanic, invisible to most visitors.

items.name: Ancient Akrotiri
items.description: The Minoan town buried in ash by the 1600 BC eruption: three-storey houses, frescoes, drainage systems. The covered site stays cool even in summer — the island's most underrated wonder.

items.name: Skaros Rock
items.description: The old fortress rock reached by a path down from Imerovigli: 360 degrees of caldera, a precipice underfoot, no trace of the crowds. The clever alternative to Oia at sunset.

items.name: Vlychada
items.description: A calm beach beneath white tuff cliffs sculpted by the wind: lunar scenery, few people, and next door an industrial museum in an old tomato factory.

items.name: Emporio
items.description: The medieval core of the island's largest village: interlocking white passages, arches and fortress houses. Tourist density near zero, photographic value infinite.

items.name: Therasia
items.description: The mini island on the caldera's far side: Santorini as it was fifty years ago. Cross by boat from Ammoudi, lunch in the stone village of Manolas, feel the clock stop.

items.name: The Akrotiri Lighthouse
items.description: The 19th-century lighthouse at the island's southwest tip: stones facing the whole caldera, wind, and a sunset that is the exact opposite of Oia's crowd.

callout.label: Morning tip
callout.text: For Oia's famous blue-dome frame, be in the village at 7 am: soft light, empty lanes, the domes yours. The same frame at noon is a selfie point with a queue.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Santorini is honest about being expensive; the real traps live between expectation and reality. Know these four.

items.name: The sunset crush at Oia's castle
items.description: Two hours before sundown the castle area becomes a festival ground; you watch the view between shoulders, on other people's phone screens.
items.instead: Skaros, the Akrotiri lighthouse, Pyrgos hill or a catamaran deck: the same sun, with room to breathe.

items.name: The donkey ride on the old-port steps
items.description: Donkeys hauling loads up hundreds of steps in the heat are the island's dark side; riding makes you part of it.
items.instead: Take the cable car or walk the steps on your own feet; a wave to the donkeys is enough.

items.name: 'Romantic sunset dinner' menu games
items.description: Some caldera restaurants sell a mediocre plate at multiplied prices as a fixed 'sunset menu'; the food is beautiful only in the photo.
items.instead: Read the menu and prices at the door; or apply the formula — dinner in the village, the glass at the view.

items.name: The cheap-ATV island tour dream
items.description: ATVs top the summer accident statistics; uninsured rentals turn scrapes into holiday-shadowing bills.
items.instead: Rent a small car or combine bus + taxi; if it must be an ATV, full insurance and a helmet are the price of entry.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: Ninety percent of Santorini's crowd stands at three points: Oia's castle, Fira's main lane, Kamari's beachfront. Step outside that triangle on the map, and the island is yours.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A full day on the caldera's rim

steps.title: Oia — before the crowds
steps.description: Blue domes, windmills and empty lanes: shoot the island's postcard in the morning's golden light.

steps.title: Down to Ammoudi
steps.description: Take the steps down to the red-cliffed port; fishing boats and morning coffee, and a swim off the rocks if you like.

steps.title: Ancient Akrotiri
steps.description: Descend to 1600 BC in the ash-buried Minoan town; read the island's real story under the cool roof.

steps.title: Vineyard lunch + tasting
steps.description: A light lunch in wine country: fava, tomatokeftedes and two glasses of Assyrtiko. Don't leave without seeing the kouloura vines.

steps.title: Village pause in Pyrgos
steps.description: Walk the kastelli lanes, look from the hilltop over both seas; coffee on the village square.

steps.title: Sunset — outside Oia
steps.description: Sit on stone at Skaros or the Akrotiri lighthouse; as the sun drops into the caldera, keep your glass full and your surroundings calm.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the island as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Caldera classics
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Oia, Ammoudi, Akrotiri, Pyrgos, sunset.

steps.title: Path and sea
steps.description: The Fira–Imerovigli–Oia caldera walk in the morning (start early), the black sand of Perivolos in the afternoon, meze in Fira at night facing the Aegean.

steps.title: The volcano's other face
steps.description: Emporio's labyrinth and Vlychada's lunar beach in the morning; by boat to Therasia or the volcano islet in the afternoon; farewell with a glass of Vinsanto.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Three words of Greek add a smile to the caldera view; five turn you from guest into friend.

items.meaning: Hello / goodbye — the formal, safe greeting
Thank you — looks hard, lands by the second try
Please / you're welcome — Greek's joker card
Cheers! — Assyrtiko glasses rise to this
'What beauty!' — it will escape you at every glance at the caldera

items.label: Walk Oia at 7 am
items.sub: Blue domes over empty lanes — the postcard is yours

items.label: Hike the Fira–Oia caldera path
items.sub: 10 km, 3–4 hours — the island's best view tour

items.label: See the ash-buried town at Akrotiri
items.sub: The Aegean's Pompeii — frescoes and three-storey houses

items.label: Taste Assyrtiko on a winery terrace
items.sub: With the caldera view; finish with Vinsanto

items.label: Eat fish at the water's edge in Ammoudi
items.sub: Under the red cliffs, by reservation

items.label: Walk out to Skaros Rock
items.sub: The path from Imerovigli — 360 degrees of caldera

items.label: Watch the sunset from outside Oia
items.sub: Lighthouse, Pyrgos or a boat deck
